operator_scope: live camera, read-only observer; no codec call, no allocation, no DNG mutation

lease.publication: rom-dcache-icache/callfn/v1, between the code write and the hook write

notes: Two defects were found and fixed while running this stage. The install survey used the claimed CODE with the stale fixed CODE_LIMIT, so it tried to read 9 KB in one mem get and every word came back omitted. And cache publication ran BEFORE the image was written, publishing an empty region; it now runs between the writes and the hook write, with a test asserting that order.
The first live arm of 2026-09-23 therefore ran with an unpublished image. It was restored without being fired.

explicitly_established.claim: the writer registers exactly one node per FHD frame: {buffer, length, kind=2}, node_next=0, and the list head is that node
the flush call at 0xC03A5490 -> 0xC069ADE0 consumes that list and returns the full 3,244,544-byte length as a 64-bit value
the flush call occupies 372 us, 0.89% of the 23.976 frame budget
the exact FHD writer shape is stable: all nine shape flags set, DNG magic present
a cave claim, ROM cache publication and a computed armed word work on the camera; the probe self-restored its hook

explicitly_not_established: that the bytes have physically reached the card when the flush returns: 3,244,544 bytes in 372 us implies 8.7 GB/s, so this is a submit or accept, not a card write
source buffer lifetime, which is the question the stage was meant to settle; the firmware's own 8-deep buffer ring is the only indication and it points the other way
shape stability across more than one frame; count is 1
flush p50/p95/p99/max, which G3 asks for and one sample cannot give
backlog growth, missed completions or double completions over a run
anything about injecting a different buffer or length into that node
